did: Asked to make release-lock form a release whenever a file home mounts changes, I read the deploy first and found it wasn't needed: envctl deploys main's own commit and treats any change under infra/ as a release of its own, so the dashboard fix from #1131 reaches home on the next make home-deploy with no new serial. I stopped and raised it instead of building. With the coordinator's go-ahead I built the one real gap instead: envctl check now refuses a mount from the release tree outside the folders the deploy reads, so that promise can't quietly break, and docs/release.md says so. I narrowed issue #1132 to match.

calls.title: Which repo paths a release-tree mount may come from
options: Only infra/ and docker-compose.yml, the trees every role's release reads
Also deploy/<role>/, which the deploy reads for that role only
calls.why: The check reads the stack once for every role, and nothing mounts from deploy/ today, so the stricter rule costs nothing and can't be wrong for a role.
calls.undo: Add the role's deploy folder to the allowed list in apps/envctl/src/mounts.rs once the check runs per role.

left: When a mount has no slash after ${REPO_ROOT}, the refusal message prints the path as if it were inside infra/, which hides the real cause. Cosmetic, so it waits for the next change to that file.
A variable merely named like REPO_ROOT, such as REPO_ROOT_EXTRA, is checked as if it were the release tree. That is stricter, not looser, and no compose file uses one.
